Q2 (shape of F-016's provenance assertion):
Read the exact call site now sitting in packages/main/src/handlers/graph.ts:
  const location = resolveGraphPackage(ctx.root);
  assertGraphRuntimeSupported(location.packageRoot);
  const lib = await import(`file://${location.entry}`) as GraphLibrary;
And confirmed isKnownBenignNonLiteralLoaderCall (retired-authority-vocabulary-guard-smoke.ts:1536-1546)
checks exactly three things and nothing else: (1) canonicalAstFingerprint(file, source.text) equals a
pinned whole-file hash, (2) enclosingFunctionName(call) textually equals the allowlisted anchor string
(here it would be the exported `graph` handler, or whatever function name encloses the call), (3)
call.arguments[0].getText(source) textually equals the allowlisted argument STRING
(`` `file://${location.entry}` ``). None of these three checks inspect what `location.entry` or
`location` itself IS, how it was produced, or what data flowed into it -- they are purely
syntactic/textual on the source of the pinned file. A mutation that keeps the literal argument text
`file://${location.entry}` unchanged but rewires `location` to come from an attacker/caller-influenced
source elsewhere (e.g. reassigning `location` from an unvalidated `--root`-adjacent path, or widening
resolveGraphPackage to accept a caller-supplied override) would pass all three checks unchanged. This
is precisely the "proves it ran vs proves it holds" gap: the guard proves the STATIC SHAPE of the call
is unchanged, not that the argument's DYNAMIC PROVENANCE is still confined to
`resolveGraphPackage()`'s own resolution logic.

Concrete assertion to make this load-bearing rather than decorative:

  A dedicated AST check -- call it `assertLoaderArgumentProvenance` (or fold into
  isKnownBenignNonLiteralLoaderCall as a second guard) -- that, for each allowlisted call site,
  additionally walks the data-flow of the pinned argument expression's ROOT IDENTIFIER back to its
  binding and asserts the binding is:
    (a) a `const` (never `let`/`var` -- rules out later reassignment before the call), AND
    (b) initialized by a call expression whose callee text is exactly the allowlisted producer
        function name (`resolveGraphPackage` for packages/main/src/handlers/graph.ts), AND
    (c) that producer function itself is defined in this same file (or another pinned file) and its
        return type/shape is not itself widened to accept an unvalidated caller-supplied override for
        the `entry` field -- concretely, assert `resolveGraphPackage`'s parameter list is unchanged
        (single `projectRoot: string` parameter, no second "entry override" parameter) as part of the
        SAME whole-file AST fingerprint that already gates admission into the allowlist map lookup.

  What it inspects: the identifier chain from `call.arguments[0]` (here `location.entry`) back through
  its member-access base (`location`) to the `const location = resolveGraphPackage(ctx.root)`
  declaration in the same function scope, verifying the initializer's callee name against a pinned
  "trusted producer" string per allowlist entry (not just the anchor function name, which only says
  WHERE the call sits, not WHERE THE ARGUMENT CAME FROM).

  What mutation it must reject: any edit that keeps the anchor name (`graph`) and the argument text
  (`` `file://${location.entry}` ``) identical, and keeps the whole-file structural fingerprint's
  OTHER 99% unchanged, but swaps the binding of `location` to originate from something other than a
  same-scope `resolveGraphPackage(...)` call -- e.g. `const location = { ...resolveGraphPackage(ctx.root), entry: args.entry ?? resolveGraphPackage(ctx.root).entry }`,
  or hoisting `location` to a parameter, or a widened `resolveGraphPackage(root, entryOverride?)`
  signature that lets a caller redirect `entry` to an arbitrary path. All of these preserve anchor +
  argument text (so the CURRENT guard passes them silently) but change what gets loaded. The
  provenance check must fail on all of them because none of them terminate the identifier's
  data-flow trace at an unparameterized, single-argument `resolveGraphPackage(ctx.root)` call in the
  same scope.

  This is exactly the class of gap F-016 originally flagged (guard proves textual/structural stability,
  not argument provenance), and the critic's confirmation that the dropped extraction "would not have
  fixed it" is consistent with this: extraction only shrinks the file that can freely mutate around the
  call, it does not add any check on what value flows into the call. The provenance assertion above is
  the actual fix; it belongs inside the guard task itself (retired-authority-vocabulary-guard-smoke.ts),
  gated on the same allowlist entries, not in graph.ts.
